newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt, Syria hold talks on Middle East peace.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, Syria hold talks on Middle East peace.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak held talks on Monday with Syria's Vice President Abdel-Halim Khaddam and Minister of Foreign Affairs Farouq al-Shara on the Middle East peace process, officials said.
Mubarak often consults Palestinian and Syrian leaders on the deadlocked peace process. He met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu last week to try to move the process ahead.

Palestinian and Israeli peace moves were thrown into crisis by the start of construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March. Palestinians say such building pre-empts final peace talks which have yet to begin in earnest.
Syria has strongly condemned Netanyahu for refusing to swap occupied Arab lands for peace and for expanding Jewish settlement in occupied areas.
Syrian-Israeli peace talks are stalled over the fate of the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967. Syria wants a full Israeli pullback from the strategic plateau.
Israel broke off peace negotiations with Syria over a year ago, before Netanyahu took office last June.
